[THALABI:v2p286#2/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | For obligations without money received, such as dowry or guarantee, the creditor must prove the debtor is solvent, since the presumption is that people are poor; absent evidence of prior means, retain the original presumption.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says a debtor who declares himself indigent is believed on oath, while creditors must establish his assets by evidence or direct observation.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abu Hanifa would detain the debtor for two or three months, inquire privately, then release him if insolvency was confirmed.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو سعيد الخدري | reports | A report from Abu Said al-Khudri supports not imprisoning an insolvent debtor: after a man lost his fruit crop and his debt grew, the Prophet said to take whatever was found, and nothing else was owed.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | As judge in Medina, Abu Hurayra refused to jail a debtor with no visible property or assets to sell; he should earn for himself and his family and repay when solvent.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | The Prophet promised that a person who goes to a debtor to collect his right receives prayers from earthly creatures, a tree in Paradise and forgiveness for every step; a debtor who delays is transgressive.
[THALABI:v2p286#2/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | The Prophet calls a solvent person’s delay in repayment injustice and instructs creditors to accept transfer to a solvent payer.
[THALABI:v2p286/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | ʿUsrah means poverty, constraint, or hardship; Abu Jaʿfar reads the word with a damma on the sin, another dialect form.
[THALABI:v2p286/r10] THALABI, d. 427 · عبد الله | reports | Abdullah’s reading is fa-nāẓirūhu ilā maysūrah; all these forms mean wealth, affluence, or spacious ease.
[THALABI:v2p286/r11] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Giving the poor debtor charity means remitting the principal owed; it is better for creditors if they know.
[THALABI:v2p286/r12] THALABI, d. 427 · عاصم | reports | Asim reads taṣṣaddaqū with a light ṣad; the other readers pronounce it doubled.
[THALABI:v2p286/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Fa-naẓirat is an imperative in the form of a declarative; the conditional fa introduces it, and its meaning is that deferment is obligatory.
[THALABI:v2p286/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The phrase means that the debtor must be given time; making it an accusative command would also be sound, like the command to strike necks.
[THALABI:v2p286/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Naẓirah means granting a delay.
[THALABI:v2p286/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو رجاء والحسن وقتادة | reports | Abu Raja, al-Hasan, and Qatada read fa-nāẓirat, a feminine participle meaning one who waits.
[THALABI:v2p286/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · عطاء بن أبي رباح | reports | Ata ibn Abi Rabah reads fa-naẓrah with a still zha; it can be a verbal noun of either looking or waiting.
[THALABI:v2p286/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · عطاء وشيبة ونافع وحميد بن محيص | reports | Ata, Shaybah, Nafi, and Humayd ibn Muhays read maysarah with a damma on the sin and tanwin.
[THALABI:v2p286/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · عمر وعلي وأبو رجاء والحسن وقتادة وعبد الله بن مسلم وأبو جعفر وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأيوب | reports | A large group of readers gives maysarah a fatha on the sin with tanwin; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer it as the common dialect.
[THALABI:v2p286/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · مجاهد وأبو سراح الهذلي | reports | Mujahid and Abu Sarrah al-Hudhali read maysarah with a damma on the sin in an annexed construction, also transmitted by Zayd from Yaqub.
[THALABI:v2p287/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | The Prophet says that whoever gives an insolvent debtor time or remits debt will be shaded by God beneath His Throne on the Day with no other shade.
[THALABI:v2p287/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عمر | reports | The Prophet says that anyone seeking an answered prayer and relief from distress should make payment easy for the insolvent.
[THALABI:v2p287/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · حذيفة بن اليمان | reports | Hudhayfa recounts that a servant’s only good deed was easing and extending time to an insolvent debtor; God says He is more entitled to do so and forgives the servant. Abu Masud testified that the Prophet had told it.
[THALABI:v2p287/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · بريدة | reports | The Prophet first promised daily charity for each day of deferment before the deadline, then charity equal to the deferred amount for each day after it; Burayda asked about the distinction.
[THALABI:v2p287/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · جابر بن عبد الله | reports | When Jabir found his debtor insolvent, he cited the verse on deferment and erased the debt record.
[THALABI:v2p288/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · عبد الله بن جعفر | reports | The Prophet says God is with a creditor until the debt is paid, provided it is not owed for something God dislikes; Abdullah ibn Jaafar consequently directed his treasurer to collect debts.
[THALABI:v2p288/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | The Prophet calls a loan taken with no intention of repayment theft.
[THALABI:v2p288/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو قتادة | reports | The Prophet initially declined to pray over a man who owed debt; Abu Qatada guaranteed repayment, so the Prophet asked whether it would be paid and then prayed. The debt was seventeen or eighteen dirhams.
[THALABI:v2p288/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو سعيد الخدري | reports | When Abu Said asked whether debt could equal disbelief, the Prophet answered yes after seeking refuge from both.
[THALABI:v2p288/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · عائشة | reports | Aisha reports that debt is God’s banner on earth: when God wills to humble a servant, He tests him with debt bound around his neck.
[THALABI:v2p288/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو هريرة | reports | After major sins, the gravest sin before God is to die owing people money with no means of repayment.
[THALABI:v2p288/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · أنس بن مالك | reports | The Prophet warns people to avoid debt because it brings anxiety at night and humiliation by day.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v1p351/r21] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | ʿUmar said the usury verse was the last Qur'anic revelation and urged people to abandon usury; the Prophet died before explaining it.

[QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r11] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The insolvent debtor has no income from assets or commercial capital; an indebtedness allotment is the only financial avenue, while one destitute in livelihood depends solely on his Master.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r12] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Return is bodily and personal at resurrection, and inward through the heart's accounting in every breath.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r13] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The present accounting and demand are more pressing than the promised reckoning that will occur at resurrection.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p127/r2] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | If he returns to those blameworthy states, he should expect near eradication and sudden punishment.

[RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One reading of ‘if you know’ makes acting on the knowledge a condition, which serves as a severe warning to those who disobey.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A second reading means if you know that charity is better than granting respite and collecting the debt.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p91/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A third reading means if you know that what your Lord commands is more beneficial for you.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Ibn Atiyya says compelling payment would apply only when the debtor is not destitute; clear poverty necessarily requires a deferment.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | If a judge sells the debtor’s property and receives the proceeds, their loss before creditors collect them is borne by creditors and discharges the debtor.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · محمد بن عبد الحكم | reports | Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam says the debtor remains liable for the proceeds until they reach the creditors.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Usra means financial hardship, nathira means delay, and maysara is a verbal noun meaning ease.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سيبويه وأبو علي | reports | Sibawayh and Abu Ali parse “dhu” as nominative because kana here is complete and means “existed” or “occurred.”
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | When debtors’ debts accumulate, a judge may take all their property while leaving necessities; Malik’s report through Ibn Nafi says only enough clothing to cover the debtor must remain.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The well-known position leaves customary clothing without surplus and preserves a cloak if removing it would humiliate the debtor.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Scholars differ on leaving clothing for the debtor’s wife and on selling books belonging to a learned person.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | A debtor is not left a dwelling, servant, or Friday clothing unless these have little value; in such circumstances detention is forbidden.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو سعيد الخدري | reports | Abu Said reports that after a fruit purchase left a man heavily indebted, the Prophet solicited donations, then told creditors to take what they found and no more.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The report establishes that the Prophet did not imprison the insolvent debtor or require creditors to keep pursuing him; Shurayh identifies the man as Muadh ibn Jabal, against the Hanafi view of detention to discover hidden assets.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وغيرهم | reports | These jurists detain a bankrupt debtor until insolvency is established; Malik does not detain one unless concealment or obstinacy is suspected, and not when genuine insolvency is verified.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#2/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | If collected assets are destroyed before sale and delivery to creditors, the debtor guarantees them and the creditors’ debts remain against him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh cites a poetic line with nominative dhu to illustrate the grammatical construction.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Qurtubi links the deferment noun to the wording “grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.” | mentions 15:36
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj allows “fanazira,” analyzing it as a verbal noun, like the forms in 56:2, 75:25, and 40:19. | mentions 56:2, 75:25, 40:19
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The phrase “and that you give charity” is the subject, and “is better” is its predicate.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السدي وابن زيد والضحاك | reports | Al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and al-Dahhak say God’s wording encourages charity to an insolvent debtor and makes it better than granting more time.

:2:280#3/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأعمش وأبو عمرو الداني عن أحمد بن موسى | reports | Al-Amash reads “if he is insolvent, then deferment”; Abu Amr al-Dani reports this reading from Ahmad ibn Musa and says it is also in Ubayy’s codex.

[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · المهدوي والنحاس | reports | Al-Mahdawi reports an Uthman codex reading with fa before “dhu hardship”; al-Nahhas reports another Uthman codex reading using accusative “dhu.”
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد وأبو رجاء والحسن | reports | The standard reading has nathira with a kasra; Mujahid, Abu Raja, and Hasan read it with a silent dh, a Tamimi dialect form comparable to their pronunciations of karam and kabid.

[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد وعطاء | reports | Mujahid and Ata are reported to read “then defer it to the matter until ease,” with a damma on the sin, kasra on the ra, and the y retained in connected speech.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#3/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو حاتم | rejects | Abu Hatim rejects the reading “fanazira,” which he says belongs only in 27:32 where a woman speaks of herself; here the word means deferment from the verb “to postpone.” | mentions 27:32
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A report promises one daily charity for each day a creditor gives an insolvent debtor respite before maturity, and double that daily reward for respite after maturity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو مسعود | reports | The Prophet recounts a wealthy man whose only good deed was ordering his servants to overlook insolvent debtors; God says He is more entitled to do so and pardons him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو قتادة | reports | After finding a debtor who had hidden, Abu Qatada heard the Prophet promise rescue from Resurrection's distress to whoever relieves an insolvent person or remits the debt.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو اليسر | reports | The Prophet says that whoever gives an insolvent debtor respite or remits the debt will be shaded by God in His shade.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | These reports explicitly encourage giving insolvent debtors relief.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Abu Qatada's report establishes that a creditor who knows or suspects the debtor's insolvency may not demand payment, even without a judge's finding of insolvency.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Giving respite means delaying collection until the debtor becomes solvent; remission means cancelling the debt from the debtor's liability.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280#4/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Abu al-Yusr combined respite and remission: he erased the debt record and told the debtor to repay if able, otherwise he was released from the debt.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | When Thaqif demanded principal from Banu al-Mughira, the latter pleaded poverty and asked to wait until their harvest; this verse was revealed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Together with 2:279, the verse establishes a creditor’s right to demand principal and take the debtor’s property without consent; the debtor must therefore repay when able. | mentions 2:279
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · بعض العلماء ومكي وابن عطية | reports | Some scholars say the verse abrogated the pre-Islamic practice of selling insolvent debtors; Makki says the Prophet ordered that practice early in Islam, and Ibn Atiyya says abrogation follows only if that Prophetic act is established.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطحاوي | reports | Al-Tahawi says a free person who lacked property could be sold for debt in early Islam until this verse abrogated the practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A report used as evidence says a debtor was brought to the Prophet, who found no property and sold him for the debt; al-Bazzar transmits a longer version, but Muslim ibn Khalid and Ibn al-Baylamani are not reliable proof.

[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع بن خثيم | prefers | Al-Nahhas prefers the view of Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym: every insolvent person is granted time in usury and all debts; this combines the positions, and the nominative reading supports generality.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:280/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس وشريح | reports | Ibn Abbas and Shurayh limit the deferment rule to usury; for other debts and transactions, the debtor must pay or may be imprisoned until payment.
[QURTUBI-FULL:4:6/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عطاء والزهري | reports | Ata, al-Zuhri, and Kufan jurists say a wife cannot seek separation for her husband's poverty and should await payment as a court debt; they cite the respite for an insolvent debtor and the encouragement to marry the poor. | mentions 2:280, 24:32

[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · نافع وحمزة | reports | They read maysarah with a damma on the sīn; both vocalizations are Arabic variants.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r11] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Both forms are also read in annexation with the tāʾ omitted, as in the cited wording from 9:77. | mentions 9:77
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r12] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Giving charity means writing off the debt; ʿAsim reads the ṣād with a light pronunciation.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r13] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Forgiving the debt is more rewarded than granting time, or better than the amount received because its reward is multiplied and lasting.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r14] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · النبي | reports | The source cites a Prophetic report that a Muslim creditor who postpones a due debt receives charity for every day of delay.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The verse can mean that a debtor has fallen into hardship; an alternate reading makes the debtor “one who has hardship.”
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | “Then deferment” can be a ruling, an obligation upon creditors, or a command that it be a deferment.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:279-280/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A reading can say that the creditor is waiting for payment or is the one granting respite; another is an imperative to grant respite.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | If a debtor is insolvent, the ruling or command is to grant time until solvency; maysara has two language forms, one read by Nafi'.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · عاصم | reports | Asim reads the verb with lightening, meaning creditors remit all or part of the principal for an insolvent debtor; other readers use the assimilated, doubled form.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The light reading omits one of the two tāʾs; the heavier reading assimilates them.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Another interpretation takes charity to mean granting the insolvent debtor more time; a Prophetic report says delaying an owed debt earns charity for every day.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#2/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | If people know this is better for them and fail to act, they are treated as if they do not know.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p716/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | عسرة means lack of money and tight circumstances, نظرة means postponement, and ميسرة means ease.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh is reported to deny مَفْعَل among singular forms, though مهلك is transmitted with three vowels; al-Kisai allows a singular مَفْعَل without contradicting Sibawayh because rare forms are not counted.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس وشريح | reports | Ibn Abbas and Shurayh say the creditor's obligation to defer payment applies specifically to usury debts.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p718/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو هريرة والحسن وعطاء والضحاك والربيع بن خثيم وعامة الفقهاء | reports | Abu Hurayra, al-Hasan, Ata, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, and most jurists say the rule covers every insolvent debtor, whether or not the debt arose from usury.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p719/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The good in giving charity is beautiful praise in this world and a great reward in the next.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النحاس | rejects | Al-Naḥḥās rejects the ḍamma because he says the pattern mafʿila occurs in only a few words and mufʿal does not occur in ordinary usage.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī allows mufʿal among singulars and cites makaraman and maʿūnan; most grammarians instead analyze these apparent examples as plurals.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · عدي | reports | ʿAdī’s verse supplies maʾlakan as another example offered for the disputed pattern.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:280#3/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النحويون | rejects | Grammarians fault Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ for reading maysarahu with a genitive pronoun because they assume mufʿal cannot be singular; the author replies that it can be a plural of maysara or a feminine form with its tāʾ omitted in annexation.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author rejects the suggestion that the ruling is limited to usury debtors: even if the passage arose in that context, its legal scope is not restricted to them.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | holds | The Shaykh answers the counterexample from laysa by saying it alone permits omission because it resembles lā; the predicate of other kāna-type verbs is doubly demanded and cannot be deleted.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · عبد الله وأبي وعثمان | reports | The readings attributed to ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy, and ʿUthmān use the accusative dhā ʿusratin, supporting the Kufan parse in which the debtor is an implicit subject.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو علي | reports | Abū ʿAlī supplies an implicit huwa as kāna’s subject, understood as the debtor from the prior discourse about a lender and borrower.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأعمش | reports | Al-Aʿmash reads in kāna muʿsiran; al-Dānī reports from Aḥmad ibn Mūsā that this wording is in ʿAbd Allāh’s codex.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | prefers | The majority retain the familiar nominative reading; Makkī says it applies to any insolvent person, whereas accusative dhā would identify a particular debtor or purchaser.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:280/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wāḥidī explains that nominative dhū ʿusratin means any insolvent person; the accusative would make the respite specific to the purchaser, though anyone in debt is entitled to it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God commands creditors to give an insolvent debtor time until he can pay, unlike the pre-Islamic creditor's demand to pay at once or increase the debt through usury.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The verse encourages a creditor to waive the entire principal and promises great good and reward for doing so.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Abu Umama reports that whoever wants God's shade on the day without shade should ease an insolvent debtor's burden or waive the debt.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Burayda reports that before a debt comes due, each day of delay earns charity equal to the debt; after it falls due, each day of delay earns double that amount.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p717#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Abu Qatada found his debtor hiding because he was insolvent; he wept and reported the Prophet's promise of the Throne's shade for one who relieves or erases a debtor's obligation. Muslim records it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | A man who eased solvent buyers and delayed insolvent ones is told by God that He is more entitled to ease and is admitted to Paradise; Bukhari, Muslim, and Ibn Majah transmit it, with Muslim adding Uqba ibn Amir and Abu Masud to the report.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | A merchant instructed his servants to overlook insolvent buyers in hope that God would overlook him, and God forgave him.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Sahl ibn Hunayf reports that helping a fighter, an insolvent debtor, or an enslaved person buying freedom earns God's shade on the day without shade; al-Hakim calls its chain sound and says the two collectors did not include it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | Al-Hakim grades the Sahl ibn Hunayf report's chain as sound and notes that Bukhari and Muslim did not record it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Ibn Umar reports that someone seeking an answered prayer and relief from distress should ease an insolvent debtor; Ahmad alone transmits the report.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p718/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | Ibn Kathir notes that Ahmad alone transmits the Ibn Umar report.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Abu Masud reports a man who could name no good deed except easing solvent buyers and delaying insolvent ones; God says He is more entitled to do so and forgives him. Muslim also transmits this through Abu Malik Saad ibn Tariq.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | Ibn Kathir says the route for the Imran ibn Husayn report is unusual and notes that a similar report from Burayda was given earlier.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Imran ibn Husayn reports that each day a creditor delays a debt owed by someone earns charity equal to the debt.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Abu al-Yusr reports that delaying an insolvent debtor or waiving the debt earns God's shade on the day without shade; Muslim transmits another route through Ubada ibn al-Walid.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p719/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو اليسر | reports | When his debtor admitted insolvency and explained he feared lying or breaking a promise, Abu al-Yusr erased the debt record and released him if unable to pay, then testified that he heard the Prophet promise divine shade for delaying or waiving a debt.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Uthman reports that God shades a person who delays an insolvent debtor or releases a debtor from what is owed.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | Ibn Abbas reports promises for delaying or waiving an insolvent person's debt, including protection from Hell; the report also says Paradise's deeds are arduous, Hell's deeds easy, the fortunate are protected from trials, and restraining anger fills the heart with faith.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p720/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · رسول الله | reports | A second Ibn Abbas report says that God will grant respite regarding a debtor's sin until the debtor repents if the creditor delays payment until the debtor can pay.
[BURHAN:v1p15/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Because early authorities’ full interpretation was not transmitted, later readers need tafsīr even more: they lack direct command of the language and must learn it.
[BURHAN:v1p15/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Tafsīr expands concise wording, uncovers meanings, and weighs possible readings in light of eloquence; it therefore needs a general method covering vocabulary, constructions, context, and outward and inward senses.
[BURHAN:v1p15/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · القاضي شمس الدين الخويى | reports | Al-Khūʾī calls tafsīr difficult because definitive knowledge of divine intent normally requires hearing it from the Prophet, which is unavailable except for a few verses; interpreters infer by signs and proofs.
[BURHAN:v1p15/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · القاضي شمس الدين الخويى | reports | Al-Khūʾī says God intended people to reflect on the Qur’an rather than receive every meaning explicitly; the Prophet’s approval of several exegetes proves interpretation without direct transmission permissible.
[BURHAN:v1p15/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · القاضي شمس الدين الخويى | reports | Al-Khūʾī criticizes writers who boast of not reading earlier books: without comparison they cannot judge the merit of their own or others’ work; good comes through God and study of the righteous, while weakness comes from the self.
[BURHAN:v1p283/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | reports | The familiar position is that the Qur’an was revealed in the Quraysh dialect.

[BURHAN:v1p283/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · أبو الأسود الدؤلى | reports | Abū al-Aswad says it was revealed in the speech of the two Kaʿbs, ancestors of Quraysh and Khuzāʿa; Khālid ibn Salama instead names both tribes because they shared a home.

[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The passage indicates that some will not abandon usury after it is prohibited, since they were not among those who believed.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Forgiving the debt is better for creditors in this world through blessing and compensation and in the next through abundant reward.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The conditional “if you know” challenges those who claim knowledge to recognize the truth and act; otherwise their refusal is crooked ignorance.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r12] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | Whoever dedicates himself to knowledge sees that relinquishing the whole debt is better than taking a portion of the good due.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r13] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها | reports | According to al-Bukhari, when the final verses, or in a variant the final verses of al-Baqara on usury, were revealed, the Prophet recited them to people in the mosque and then prohibited trade in wine.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r14] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما | reports | Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's statement that the final verse revealed to the Prophet was the usury verse.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r15] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · ابن شهاب | reports | Abū ʿUbayd transmits Ibn Shihāb's report that the last Qur'anic material entrusted at the Throne was the verses of usury and debt. | mentions 2:282
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | War is forceful resistance over what one refuses to yield; here it conveys the severity of resisting the demand to give up usury.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Mention of God and His Messenger magnifies the threat through God's grandeur and the Messenger's honor by association with Him.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | The Messenger was prepared for mercy, so the Prophet of mercy becomes an adversary to the usurer, severing the usurer's connection to the Merciful and intercessor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | If debtors repent by stopping the remaining usury, the creditors retain their original principal, as in a sale.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Neither side should be wronged: creditors must not take the usurious excess, and debtors must not reduce the principal or delay payment unjustly.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | A debtor in hardship who cannot presently pay must be granted deferment until ease if the creditors insist on recovering their money.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | A deferment is a delay whose completion is awaited.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p541/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza read maysarah with a ḍamma on sīn, signaling the fullest ease; others read it with fatḥa, signaling an intermediate ease, so waiting for the broadest ease is more virtuous.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · البراء بن عازب وزيد بن أرقم | reports | The Prophet allowed currency exchange when hand-to-hand and forbade it when deferred.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet forbade trading fresh dates for dried dates after confirming that fresh dates lose weight when dried.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · أبو بكر الصديق | reports | The Prophet warned that exchanging gold or silver for its own kind at a surplus places both the demander and the one supplying extra in the Fire.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r4] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · أبو بكرة | reports | Abu Bakra reports that the Prophet forbade currency exchange two months before his death.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reports that the verse about granting respite to an insolvent debtor was revealed concerning usury.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | The command to delay applies to an insolvent person in usury, not to a trust, which must be returned to its owners. | mentions 4:58
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | In the usury context, “and that you remit it” means forgiving the debt owed by an insolvent person.
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · شريح | reports | When urged not to imprison an insolvent debtor, Shurayh held that this verse concerns usury among an Ansar group; ordinary trusts must instead be delivered as 4:58 commands. | mentions 4:58
[DURR-FULL:v2p111#2/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | The insolvent person in the verse is the debtor who is being pursued for payment.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · السدي | reports | The debtor receives respite on the principal until becoming wealthy; remitting the principal to a poor debtor is charity, and al-Abbas did so.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الضحاك | reports | The rule covers every debt owed by a Muslim: do not imprison or demand payment from a debtor known to be insolvent until God grants ease; forgiving principal is better than waiting, and God prefers charity.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Forgiving an insolvent person's debt brings greater reward; declining to forgive is not sinful, but imprisoning an insolvent is sinful, and a debtor able to pay who refuses is recorded as unjust.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r4] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Whoever gives an insolvent debtor more time or remits the debt will be sheltered by God on the Day when there is no shade but His.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A wealthy man who eased payment for those able to pay and delayed the insolvent was forgiven when God said He was more entitled to show such generosity.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A creditor who delays collecting a right receives charity for each day of delay.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | To have supplications answered and distress removed, a person should relieve an insolvent debtor.
[DURR-FULL:v2p113/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Whoever delays an insolvent debtor until he can pay will have God delay his punishment until the debtor repents.
[DURR-FULL:v2p115/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A wealthy man with no other good deeds regularly told his servants to overlook insolvent debtors, and God said He was more entitled to that generosity and forgave him.
[ITQAN:v2p393/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · الشافعي وابن جرير وأبو عبيدة والقاضي أبو بكر وابن فارس | reports | Most authorities deny foreign-origin words in the Quran, citing its description as Arabic; al-Shafiʿi strongly rebukes the claim, while Ibn Faris argues foreign vocabulary would explain away the Arabs’ failure to match it. | mentions 12:2, 41:44
[ITQAN:v2p393/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abu ʿUbayda says the Quran was revealed in clear Arabic and calls it an extreme claim to say it contains non-Arabic words such as كذابا in Nabataean.
[ITQAN:v2p393/r3] ITQAN, d. 911 · ابن جرير | reports | Ibn Jarir explains reports that Ibn ʿAbbas and others called Quranic terms Persian, Abyssinian, or Nabataean as words shared across languages, not borrowed vocabulary.
[ITQAN:v2p393/r4] ITQAN, d. 911 · آخرون | reports | Another view allows foreign-origin terms that Arab travelers borrowed, altered, and assimilated into their own eloquent speech before the Quran used them.
